claims.text: A transient liquid-phase sintering agent with a eutectic temperature below 800 °C will enable rapid densification of the Mg-transition-metal powder mixture within 800–1000 °C.
The transient liquid-phase agent will homogenize the Mg-transition-metal mixture.
Liquid-phase sintering will suppress elemental volatility in the proposed temperature window.
Liquid-phase sintering will prevent microstructural instability by bypassing solid-state diffusion limitations.
The initial Mg-transition-metal powder mixture has inherent segregation tendencies and unstable microstructures.
Standard sintering currently fails to produce high density or corrosion resistance in the proposed mixture.
An Mg-Si or Mg-Al-Si low-melting agent can induce transient liquid-phase sintering in the proposed material.
Controlled heating at 850–900 °C is the proposed optimum processing range.
Optimizing the heating rate will minimize Mg vaporization.
A controlled atmosphere will prevent oxidation during the liquid-phase stage.
The transient liquid phase facilitates rapid particle rearrangement and solution-precipitation.
Particle rearrangement and solution-precipitation will produce a homogeneous, single-phase-like matrix with suppressed grain growth.
The liquid phase lowers the activation energy for mass transport.
Solid-state diffusion is too slow to achieve adequate densification at the relevant temperatures without a liquid phase.
A short liquid-state dwell prevents excessive Mg volatility and elemental segregation.
The proposed process will produce an alloy exceeding 95% theoretical density.
The proposed alloy will have a uniform microstructure, significantly improved oxidation and corrosion resistance, and no detectable segregation or porosity.
Standard solid-state sintering at 800–1000 °C produces low relative density, porous microstructures, incomplete diffusion, segregation, and poor functional properties.
Above 1000 °C, density fails because rapid Mg volatility and pore coarsening occur.
Below 800 °C without a liquid phase, Mg volatility occurs and prevents densification.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that Mg volatility occurs when temperature drops below 800 °C, whereas the mechanism and processing conditions frame volatility primarily as a high-temperature or excessive-dwell problem. No explanation is provided for why lowering temperature below 800 °C would itself cause volatility.
